newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds slip in thin trade, await data.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds slip in thin trade, await data.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities fell into a virtual slumber with Treasuries on Tuesday afternoon, traders said.
"We're in a pretty thin range here and there are not a lot of bonds trading," said one trader at a U.S. investment firm based in New York.
Most prices of pass-throughs were 1/32 to 2/32 lower, while comparable Treasuries slipped 1/32 to 2/32 as well.
The post-Presidents' Day session has been "very quiet" amid a dearth of economic data, said another trader. No mortgage banker selling was seen either, he said.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent issues were 1/32, at 100-28/32, yielding 112 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper was off 1/32 as well, at 100-22/32 and 100-27/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note was also down 3/32 at 99-25/32 to yield 6.28 percent.
The Consumer Price Index report is slated for release on Wednesday at 0830 EST/1330 GMT.

On average, economists forecast overall CPI rose 0.3 percent in January versus a 0.3 percent gain the previous month. The core CPI index, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, was seen up 0.2 percent in January.
